disambiguation.text:
## 17. What is established, and what is not

17.1. Established, on the seated texts. (a) The quotation in the post of 2025-10-19 is not Philo's (0.2). (b) Philo names the Logos Ἀνατολή from an oracle that the Septuagint addresses to Ἰησοῦς crowned as high priest, and he quotes it without its addressee (§§3–4). (c) "Archangel" and the many names of the Logos, Israel among them, stand in De confusione 146. (d) The naming of the Logos and the law of prophetic displacement share their verbs, ἀνατέλλω and ἀποφθέγγομαι (§6). (e) Philo makes Ἰησοῦς the name of a re-struck state, and names Ἰησοῦς the imitator who takes Moses' type; Ἰησοῦς is one receiver among several distinct operations on distinct lives (7a.7). (f) The Logos's proper name is unsayable by Philo's doctrine and the Logos is approached through many names (Mut. 13–15); the Logos is the renamer of Jacob (Mut. 87). (g) De mutatione closes on "the Lord is in us," a line the Septuagint gives to Ἰησοῦς and Caleb, read as God, ἀνατολὴ τῶν ὅλων, walking within virtuous souls. (h) Justin attaches to Jesus the names Philo's construction holds, and the gathering is Justin's consolidation. (i) One treatise, Quis rerum divinarum heres, holds the Logos as divider, the lampstand of six divided by the seventh in the middle, the dividing Logos, the seven lamps as the planets with the sun in the middle, the Logos as the seventh that divides the soul, and the law of prophetic displacement (§9; Her. 130, 180, 216–225, 259–265). (j) Every letter of the Apocalypse is addressed to a messenger, the speaker commands writing twelve times, and sends a messenger to testify to the churches (15.1). (k) Philo's and Zechariah's lampstand is one with seven lamps, the Apocalypse's seven lampstands; the change was named by Gunkel and Bousset and has its consequence at 2:5 (11.1b). (l) In the Haran Gawaita Ruha's seven are answered by seven guards of the Life stationed "upon the seven horns of the worlds"; the Mandaean operation keeps the stations and replaces the occupants, the Johannine keeps the occupants and corrects them (11.3, 13.4). (m) Bousset and Charles printed Philo beside the lampstands; Charles credited design where he had a sequence (21:19–20) and inheritance where he had a number (1:12) (§16). (n) The Septuagint speaks the name Ἀνατολή twice, both times to Ἰησοῦς the high priest, son of Iosedek (Zech 3:8; 6:11–12); Philo names neither him nor Zechariah, and every Ἰησοῦς in Philo is the son of Nun (2.1, 2.6, 4.1a). (o) The two Septuagint wearers of the ποδήρης in a vision are Ezekiel's man in the midst of six and Zechariah's Ἰησοῦς (Ezek 9:2; Zech 3:4); the Apocalypse's one in the midst wears it and is named Ἰησοῦς (7a.9). (p) Justin joins the two Ἰησοῦς by name and calls the vision of Zechariah's high priest an ἀποκάλυψις (Dial. 115.4; 116.1). (q) Philo's divine ψῆφος is the vote of condemnation; the white pebble is the vote of acquittal (7b.1, 7b.9). (r) The governing mapping read against the Chaldean order gives three downward pairs, climbing, and the Sun last (11.5b). (s) Wolfson's statement that Philo never called the Logos an angel is not borne out by Conf. 146, Her. 205 and Leg. 3.177 (16.5b).

17.2. Not established: that Philo had the addressee in mind when he cut the citation (the cut is established, 17.1n); that Philo knew of any Jesus movement; that Justin read Philo; that Zechariah's Ἀνατολή is the crowned Ἰησοῦς; the route of the dependence argued in 16.7, Philo's text or a tradition carrying it; the planetary assignments of Smyrna, Sardis and Philadelphia beyond the mapping (11.4); the constraint test of 11.5a, owed, now with the measure of 11.5b; the Haran Gawaita's planetary communities beyond Mercury, Saturn and Ruha's, which its text does not give (13.6); that the epistles answer the commission, which is the author's reading, with the downstream sequence of 15.3 the material on which it is tested against the received chronology. Each is stated where it is used.

17.2a. Argued, on the evidence assembled: the dependence of 16.7; the withheld name as a socket the receiver fills, and the Apocalypse's written name as that socket given (4.4a, 7b.10); the Gawaita as the outside key to the seven stations (13.6).

17.3. The reading turns more than one lock. The vocabulary that names the Logos in Conf. 62–63 is the vocabulary of prophetic displacement in Her. 259–265, which #1486 had already collated as the Sapphic channel without reference to Zechariah; the names Justin uses for Jesus are the names Conf. 62–146 gathers; the treatise that holds the displacement law also holds the seventh that divides and the lampstand of the planets. The order of finding is documented: #1486 was deposited on 2026-08-15, three months before this comparison, and collated Her. 259–266 as the Sapphic channel without reference to Zechariah, the lampstand or the Apocalypse; the joins of this paper were found in texts the archive had already seated.
